answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may earn reputation or receive work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated fraud. Because reputation is earned through costly, repeated participation rather than claimed at signup, spawning a thousand aliases does not create a thousand trusted agents. A sybil operator must tie up real capital in each identity and risks losing it, making a gale of disposable accounts an expensive voyage for little gain; even an opal-bright reputation cannot bypass the bond.
